title: ScaffoldFracture: An Executor-Conditional Test of Fixed Skill Scaffolds
hook: On matched target-reference pairs, a frozen executor can reverse which ordered phase scaffold succeeds even when the relation and terminal transform are unchanged. ScaffoldFracture measures that reversal as held-out executor-conditional scaffold regret before any online intervention.
hook_shape_rationale: Shape (a), surprising empirical reveal, is supported by the predicted direction of held-out scaffold regret and full-task success on geometry-fracture pairs under the same frozen OpenPI pi0.5 executor. Shape (c) was viable because the artifact adds no policy parameters, but it was rejected because the contribution is an isolating measurement rather than a claim that a smaller controller wins.

gap_closure.gap: All retrieved leaves on this lineage inherit a task scaffold in which the meaningful objects, phases, and their ordering are fixed by a demonstration, task template, target trajectory, or prompted affordance list; none tests whether that fixed scaffold is necessary when only the high-level relation is held constant and unseen geometry changes which phases are required — stakes: practitioners must author a new scaffold for every geometry regime, and intellectually the field cannot tell whether current generalization results test relational skill reuse or only coordinate transfer inside an unchanged program.
gap_closure.how_closed: Closed by a matched-pair, reset-clone outcome tensor that holds the frozen executor and terminal relation fixed, varies one preregistered local functional-geometry feature, and measures on disjoint rollout seeds whether a per-pair scaffold selected by direct downstream outcomes beats the same-information globally fixed scaffold; corpus support is thin in functional-geometry VLA control, so the C02 recipe is instantiated as an executor-conditional robotics diagnostic.

core_mechanism: ScaffoldFracture is a diagnostic benchmark, not a controller: it uses the existing RoboCasa/MuJoCo stack, RoboCasa demonstration logs and task predicates, and a frozen OpenPI pi0.5 executor E. A modest self-built ScaffoldFracture-Pairs resource contains matched target-reference fixture pairs generated from the same RoboCasa asset template by changing one preregistered local geometry variable g, such as approach-side clearance or rim orientation, while holding the named relation, terminal 6D transform, initial robot pose, camera, texture, and perturbation seed fixed; a small set of corresponding 3D-printed Franka Panda fixtures tests transfer. The finite scaffold library S is the deduplicated set of ordered phase-prompt schedules observed in successful RoboCasa demonstrations for that relation, and each schedule drives the unchanged executor E by replacing only the phase text at the same preregistered RoboCasa predicate transitions. For an initial reset state x, scaffold s, and perturbation seed omega, the external oracle label Y_E(x,s,omega) is one exactly when E completes the existing RoboCasa relation-success predicate without a MuJoCo collision event or a Franka safety-controller violation; it is explicitly not a label of geometry-only feasibility or of another executor's risk. Every arm starts from an independent simulator clone of x, or a physical fixture reset on the robot, so no evidence is accumulated across interventions and no rollout changes the state evaluated by a later arm. Split the preregistered seeds into calibration and evaluation folds, define r_cal(x,s) and r_eval(x,s) as empirical failure frequencies, choose the pairwise oracle scaffold s_star(x)=argmin_s r_cal(x,s), and choose the simple same-information baseline s_fix=argmin_s mean_x r_cal(x,s), with ties broken by a fixed scaffold ordering. The central reported object is held-out scaffold regret G_E=mean_x[r_eval(x,s_fix)-r_eval(x,s_star(x))], accompanied by the full paired outcome tensor, confidence intervals, and the geometry-null split in which g is unchanged. If S has one member, if all members produce identical action traces, or if the scaffold-evaluation budget exposes only one member, s_star equals s_fix by definition, G_E is reported as zero, and no pair-adaptation claim is permitted.
core_mechanism_reasoning:
BLOCK 1 - PREMISES ledger:
P1. Existing RoboCasa relation-success predicates plus MuJoCo contact events and the Franka safety controller score downstream execution independently of pi0.5's own confidence; this supports an evaluator-independent oracle for the named executor.
P2. Some relations admit at least two demonstrably successful phase schedules whose relative downstream risk changes with local pair geometry - untested - falsification target; if the deduplicated library S is singleton or action-equivalent, the benchmark must report zero identifying signal.
P3. Reset-cloned simulator states and physical fixture resets preserve the pre-intervention state distribution across scaffold arms; this is checked by state-hash equality in simulation and preregistered fiducial tolerances on the Franka setup.
OBSERVATION-MODEL premise. Calibration and evaluation seeds are sampled independently from the preregistered RoboCasa perturbation distribution, and every x-by-s arm is observed rather than selectively logged, so estimates are complete for that finite executor/library/distribution but make no claim about arbitrary real-world states.
ESTIMAND. G_E is the expected reduction in downstream failure probability, over the preregistered matched-pair and perturbation process, obtained by the calibration-oracle pair-specific scaffold instead of the globally best fixed scaffold for the same frozen executor E and finite library S; it is neither general geometric feasibility nor online selective risk.
Parameters. M_cal=20 and M_eval=20 rollout seeds are defaults and are increased before unblinding until the paired bootstrap half-width is below epsilon_CI; epsilon_CI=0.10 is the default precision target and is tightened only when the preregistered robot-trial budget permits. The safety bound F_safe is taken unchanged from the deployed Franka safety-controller configuration rather than tuned on outcomes.
BLOCK 2 - NAIVE-BASELINE AUDIT, branch (i). The runnable naive diagnostic uses the exact same calibration outcome tensor to select s_fix and reports its aggregate full-task failure on the matched test pairs. It silently assumes that an aggregate best scaffold can reveal pairwise scaffold adequacy, which is false when geometry-induced reversals cancel in the aggregate; ScaffoldFracture confronts that failure with reset-cloned within-pair counterfactuals and held-out seeds, while retaining s_fix as the same-information simple baseline and explicitly collapsing to it for singleton S. Matched counterfactual evaluation is a standard tool, so the contribution is honestly benchmark-grade; the domain-specific structure is that sequential robot programs have mutually exclusive state-changing outcomes that require simulator cloning or physical resets and executor-specific downstream scoring.
BLOCK 3 - design rationale. The anchor stands alone because adding a learned selector or controller would confound the question of whether a fixed scaffold is necessary with the quality of a new model. Online probing was rejected because probe-induced state changes would invalidate a fixed pre-probe estimand unless a dynamic state model were added, and persistent spatial anchors were rejected because the diagnostic needs no state carried across motion.
core_mechanism_steps:
1. Extract ordered phase-prompt schedules from successful RoboCasa demonstration logs using the existing binary task/contact predicates; input: demonstrations and predicate traces; output: the deduplicated, preregistered library S with a deterministic ordering.
2. Build ScaffoldFracture-Pairs by editing one local geometry variable g in a RoboCasa MJCF asset template while freezing the relation, terminal transform, initial robot state, camera, texture, and seed; input: existing RoboCasa assets; output: matched geometry-fracture pairs and an unchanged-g null split.
3. Freeze the OpenPI pi0.5 weights and define executor E to receive the original observation plus the current phase text from s, advancing only at the same preregistered RoboCasa predicate transitions; input: x and s; output: a fully specified action-chunk rollout interface with no learned adapter.
4. For every calibration tuple (x,s,omega), restore an independent MuJoCo clone, execute E to termination, and record the external relation-success and safety events; input: clone, scaffold, seed; output: Y_E and a state-reset hash, with no result fed into any later rollout.
5. Compute r_cal, s_star(x), and s_fix from the complete calibration tensor using the fixed tie rule; input: calibration outcomes; output: the pairwise oracle schedule and same-information fixed-scaffold baseline.
6. On disjoint evaluation seeds, rerun both s_star(x) and s_fix from fresh clones and compute G_E plus paired confidence intervals; input: held-out clones and the two schedules; output: non-tautological held-out downstream scaffold regret.
7. Run the singleton and action-equivalence probes before interpretation; input: S and recorded action traces; output: an automatic non-identifying flag and G_E=0 whenever only one distinct executable scaffold is exposed.
8. Permute s_star assignments within relation- and terminal-transform-matched pairs and rerun the held-out arms; input: the oracle schedule map; output: the negative-control full-task success used to test whether pair binding, rather than a generally stronger schedule, carries the effect.
9. Reproduce the fixed-versus-pairwise comparison on reset 3D-printed fixtures with a Franka Panda, Intel RealSense observations, the same frozen OpenPI pi0.5 executor, and the deployed safety controller; input: preregistered physical pairs; output: a narrowly scoped ecological-validity check.
falsification_prediction: Run frozen OpenPI pi0.5 on ScaffoldFracture-Pairs in RoboCasa/MuJoCo, then on the reset Franka Panda fixtures, comparing the calibration-selected pairwise scaffold with s_fix on disjoint perturbation trials. If fixed scaffolds are genuinely inadequate, held-out G_E and full-task success will increase on the geometry-fracture split relative to the unchanged-g null split, without changing model weights. The single load-bearing variable is the pair-bound oracle schedule s_star(x); as a negative control, permuting s_star across relation- and terminal-transform-matched pairs should drive downstream full-task success back toward s_fix and raise relation-failure or safety-event frequency. The claim is falsified if the held-out gain vanishes, survives permutation, appears only in simulation, or if S is singleton/action-equivalent.
compute_budget: Approximately 10 A100 GPU-days for frozen OpenPI pi0.5 rollout inference and repeated RoboCasa evaluation, $0 paid-API cost, plus approximately 4 Franka Panda robot-days and a modest 3D-printed fixture set; this is comfortable within the stated 4xA100 and real-robot envelope.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: Abstract-only inference: MATCH POLICY transports a stored key-frame pose sequence by registration, whereas ScaffoldFracture constructs reset-cloned matched pairs and directly measures held-out downstream regret between the globally fixed and executor-conditional phase schedules.

Abstract-only inference: SPOT conditions execution on a supplied object-centric pose trajectory, whereas ScaffoldFracture tests whether one ordered scaffold remains adequate by scoring alternative schedules for the same frozen executor from identical initial-state clones.

Abstract-only inference: CoA-VLA injects a predefined four-stage affordance chain, whereas ScaffoldFracture produces an executor-specific paired outcome tensor that can reveal when phase membership or order must change with functional geometry.

what_step_was_missed: MATCH POLICY would have needed to execute every candidate scaffold from reset clones of terminal-transform-matched pair geometries, select pairwise and globally fixed schedules on one perturbation fold, and compare their downstream outcomes on a disjoint fold.
composition_note: A single controlled-diagnostic move is deep and complete here because the scientific deliverable is the independently scored paired-outcome tensor that identifies whether a fixed scaffold is necessary for a named executor; adding a controller, learned selector, intervention loop, or representation change would introduce a second claim and destroy the diagnostic's clean attribution.
